title: A horn is a plane spiral only if fastest and slowest growth lie diametrically opposite

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A horn is a plane spiral only if fastest and slowest growth lie diametrically opposite

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: If the maximal and minimal growth rates around the basal growth zone of a horn lie diametrically opposite, the horn is a plane spiral; otherwise it is a spiral in space with a helical component, which is the usual case because the horn's field of force has no such plane of symmetry.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: plane spiral iff the maximal and minimal growth rates around the base lie at \Delta\phi = 180^\circ; otherwise helicospiral

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: The Shapes of Horns, and of Teeth or Tusks: with a Note on Torsion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: If the maximal and minimal velocities of growth be precisely at opposite sides of the zone of growth, the resultant spiral will be a plane spiral; but if they be not precisely or diametrically opposite, then the spiral will be a spiral in space, with a winding or helical component

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIII, “The Shapes of Horns, and of Teeth or Tusks: with a Note on Torsion”; topic “Summary of horn growth”. Scope: horns of ruminants

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: plane spiral iff the maximal and minimal growth rates around the base lie at \Delta\phi = 180^\circ; otherwise helicospiral

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch13-06: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction is mathematically operational, but its crucial independent variable is a developing basal growth field. Final horn shapes alone cannot establish where growth maxima and minima lay.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure circumferential growth-rate fields at the horn base through time and test whether diametrically opposed extrema predict zero torsion while offset extrema predict a helical component. The predicted relationship across developing horns would support the law; discordant growth fields and trajectories would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Longitudinal developmental imaging of horn growth appears necessary.

Public collections provide final form, not spatially resolved growth velocities.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a geometric rule linking the position of fastest and slowest growth to planarity, and it is testable when growth bands can be read around the horn. Existing 3D archives record the resulting curve much more often than the increment field that is supposed to cause it. A subset of photographed sheaths with clear rings could be measured, but a family-wide test would require new digitizing of increment positions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Around the basal growth zone, map which side of the horn thickened fastest using growth-line spacing or sheath increments, and relate the angular separation of the maximum and minimum to whether the centerline is planar. The claim is confirmed if planarity occurs when those extrema are opposite and a helical component appears when they are offset; it is refuted if planar horns regularly have offset extrema.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Circumferential growth-rate maps are rarely digitized; most archives store overall shape only.

If the extrema are inferred from the centerline, the test repeats the geometric definition.
